name: 09_tail_clause
description: S1 is redeemed at k × D_avg = 150 (tail cap 82.5 per unit); a liquidity event reported inside the 12-month tail pays holders at redemption up to the tail cap (excess refunded), a later event finds the cap exhausted, and reports after the tail window are rejected. S2 was redeemed at its remaining cap, so no tail is ever due.

config.chainDomainNote: Bid/ask commitments, signed messages and the deployment domain depend on chain-specific wallet bytes and chain id; harnesses recompute them from the plaintext fields here (salts, prices, quantities, periods, nonces) and sign with the keys derived from `keys[*].seed`. Amounts, periods and ledger values are chain-independent.

steps.note: k × D_avg = 5 × 30 = 150 decides; tail cap = 232.5 − 150 = 82.5 per unit
b4 has not claimed yet: still holds 100 units, redeemedUnits 0
a report on a Redeemed series must flag a liquidity event
exit: owed 4% × 920,000 = 36,800 (units public input = units at redemption = 400)
tail cap 82.5 × 400 = 33,000 accepted; 3,800 refunded; fee 1,650; tailAccWad = 31,350 / 400 per unit
tail distributed; refundedToIssuer unchanged (tail refunds are tracked in the tail state)
b4 must claim the redemption first so its redeemed units are recorded
each holder received 7,837.5 USDC of tail; vault empty; all units burned
C_rem = 262.5 − 252 = 10.5 < hurdle → remaining cap decides, tail cap 0
S2 closed out at 10.5 per unit
another 20,000 owed, but the tail cap is exhausted
tailPaidPerUnitWad stays at the cap; issuer balance unchanged by this payment
